title: OpenFlow module profile
description: One profile for a Naya Create module (Touch, Track, Tune or Float). This is the interchange format the Modules page imports and exports; it is deliberately not the shape of the database rows. See the three examples beside this file for a real profile of each type.

format.description: Marks the document as a module profile. Optional so a hand-written file is not rejected for missing it, but an importer will refuse a file that claims to be something else.

version.description: Format version. 1 is the only one so far.

moduleType.description: REQUIRED. Which module this profile is for, and therefore which section of the module list it lands in. It is not inferred from the gestures: a Touch and a Tune share gesture names, so guessing would quietly misfile the profile.

name.description: Display name. An import that collides with an existing name is numbered rather than overwriting, so importing twice gives you two profiles to compare.

variant.description: Which stock map this descends from, e.g. TRACK_LEFT or TRACK_RIGHT. It matters for Track, which is physically asymmetric: flipping the module to the other side reverses the button order and the scroll direction, so left and right ship different default maps. Either variant can occupy either bay.

settings.description: Module settings by their correlation id, as strings (speeds, thresholds, flags). Absent when the module has none.

bindings.description: One entry per gesture, keyed by the gesture's behavior string ("tap:touch:1_finger", "vertical:tune:1_finger", "rotate:tune:dial"). Gestures the module does not have are ignored on import; a file whose gestures ALL belong to another module type is refused, on the assumption that moduleType is wrong.

actionType.description: What kind of action the code is. "none" for unbound, "key" for a keyboard or consumer usage, "mouse" for a button, "value" for a direction PAIR, "shortcut_alias" for a chord, "LED" for an action the keyboard handles internally.

actionCode.description: The action itself: "F17", "C_VOL_UP", "M1", "LGUI + TAB". A "value" code names BOTH directions of a pair, minus first: "mouse - SCROLL_UP - SCROLL_DOWN" for a motion axis, "C_VOL_DOWN - C_VOL_UP" for the dial (the leading kind is optional -- the last two parts are the two directions). Empty string means unbound.

invert.description: Swap the two directions of a pair. On the device this is a selector swap, not a stored flag.

split.description: Present only when the two halves of a direction pair are bound INDEPENDENTLY -- an axis or the dial with each direction on its own action. The combined actionCode above still names the pair, and each half here overrides one direction of it. A gesture with no `split` uses both directions of its combined code.
